title: [The Story, Distilled]
summary: Spoiler-aware statistics for The Wandering Inn: word counts, how often anything is mentioned, and every Skill the System grants.
homeBlurb: [The Story, Distilled] counts The Wandering Inn, from its seventeen million words to every Skill granted, and never shows past the chapter you have read to.
description: A statistics site for The Wandering Inn, the web serial by pirateaba. It totals words by chapter, volume and month, counts how often any character, place or phrase appears across the story, and tracks each Skill: when it was gained and how often it is used. Concepts and Skills link to the Wandering Inn Wiki.

Tell it the last chapter you have read and everything after it is hidden. It is styled as a grimoire, with drifting motes of light, a turning magic circle and Skills that glow like System text. Made with Claude.
promises: Nothing past the chapter you have read to is shown.
No chapter text is published: a search returns only counts per chapter, and every result links to the official chapter.

title: Bento
summary: Turn any JSON into a small app: drag fields onto a grid, pick how each one is shown, and run it.
homeBlurb: Bento turns a JSON file into an app, laying its fields out as tables, charts, maps and tabs on a grid.
description: Bento is a browser editor for JSON. Drop in a file, or point it at a URL or a JSON Schema, and it lists every field. Drag a field onto the grid, choose a component such as a table, chart, gauge, map, Markdown or tabs, and the app takes shape. Preview it, run it against live data, and edit values in place.
An app is itself a small JSON file, so it can be saved, exported or shared as a link that carries the app inside it. Nothing is uploaded unless you choose to include the data. Made with Claude.
promises: Bento has no server of its own: your JSON stays in your browser.
A shared link carries the app inside it, and includes your data only if you choose to.

title: Depot
summary: One desktop window for every package manager, on this computer and on your other machines: what is installed, what has updates, and what happened.
homeBlurb: Depot gathers Homebrew, the Mac App Store, npm, pipx, Cargo, winget and more into one window, reaches your other Macs and Linux machines over SSH, and shows every command it runs.
description: Depot is a desktop app for macOS and Windows that lists every package from every package manager in one place, groups pending updates by source, searches all sources at once, and keeps a history with a revert where the manager allows one. Health flags packages with known vulnerabilities or that their manager has deprecated, and Insights charts what is installed and how it changes.

It can also manage other Macs and Linux machines over SSH: Depot installs its small agent there itself, then shows that machine's packages and updates and runs installs, updates and removals on it. Windows machines are next. An AI assistant such as Claude can use Depot too, through its MCP server: off until you turn it on, read only or full access, and every change it queues shows in History.

It never changes anything except by running the package manager's own command, and each command appears in its log exactly as it was run. It is in preview (version 0.2.4) with a small group of testers, and it updates itself. Made with Claude.
promises: It never changes anything except by running the package manager’s own command.
Every command appears in its log exactly as it was run, on this computer or another machine.
It reverts only where the manager allows one.
AI assistants get no access until you turn it on.

title: Ghostcast
summary: Go live to an AI chat audience that reacts to your voice, camera, and stream moments.
homeBlurb: Ghostcast imagines a livestream with an AI audience that responds to voice, camera, and the rhythm of the room.
description: Ghostcast is a pretend livestream: turn on your camera and mic, then watch an AI-written audience react to what you say and show. Nothing is broadcast to other people.
The chat has its own rhythm, emotes, and reactions to stream events, so it feels lively even when you pause.
promises: Nothing is broadcast to other people.

title: God Is a Dick: SINfully Good
summary: A satirical cookbook of spectacularly, unapologetically non-kosher food.
homeBlurb: God Is a Dick: SINfully Good turns forbidden pairings into a full satirical cookbook.
description: A 120-page cookbook with 45 recipes that break the rules on purpose: bacon-fat challah French toast, lobster gefilte fish, cheeseburger bourekas, and plenty more.
The writing pairs Jewish food traditions with irreverent humor and practical cooking. Made with Claude and ChatGPT.

title: Dirhaven
summary: Explore your filesystem as a pixel-art town where folders become places and files become objects.
homeBlurb: Dirhaven makes a filesystem walkable, giving folders streets and files things to discover.
description: Dirhaven turns folders into districts, buildings, and rooms. Walk the map, open files as books, pictures, video, or music, and meet residents with errands that lead you through the tree.
The world is generated deterministically without an LLM, and files are read only when you choose to open them. The linked demo uses a made-up sample folder. Made with Claude.
promises: The world is generated without an LLM.
Files are read only when you choose to open them.

title: Sunder
summary: Scan a receipt, split the items fairly, and keep track of who has paid.
homeBlurb: Sunder brings the group back to earth, scanning receipts and finding fair shares.
description: Sunder extracts receipt items, lets people claim quantities or split by percentage and custom amounts, then calculates balances and tracks payments.
Shared links let a group participate without each person setting up an account. Built with Manus.
promises: People can join a split from a shared link without setting up an account.
